prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The swap-gain computation in the graph-cut partitioner recomputes cut contributions from raw adjacency but double-counts the exchanged edge (node1<->node2) because it is counted in both `node1_to_complement`/`node2_to_partition` before and again in `node1_to_partition`/`node2_to_complement` after; correcting the gain so the mutually-exchanged edge cancels exactly yields a more accurate min-cut refinement that reduces cross-tier cuts (and thus cross-tier detours), improving TNS across all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.107 robust(mean-std)=-0.107 min_case=-0.136 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.136 dWNS=-9.3% dTNS=-16.4% overflow~126
  bp-ng45: score=+0.004 dWNS=-5.4% dTNS=+4.2% overflow~115
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.025 dWNS=+1.7% dTNS=+3.0% overflow~115
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis did not hold: total score is −0.107, with only 2/3 cases improving slightly and ariane133-ng45 regressing sharply (dWNS −9.3%, dTNS −16.4%). The mechanism claim (fewer cross-tier cuts → less detour → better TNS) is contradicted by ariane's large TNS loss despite overflow ~126, suggesting the gain correction perturbs partition balance or timing-critical assignments rather than cleanly reducing cuts. bp/bp_fe gains are marginal and within noise. Next step: instrument the partitioner to log actual cut-size deltas per move and correlate with per-path timing, isolating whether the exchanged-edge cancellation changes move acceptance or just gain sign.
